result.description:
Position: Office Manager 
Office Location: 60 South Street, Ipswich QLD 4305 
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent, Minimum 38 hours a week  
Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum (plus superannuation)

Our client PRITHVEER PTY LTD is an established Australian transport and logistics provider based out of Ipswich, Queensland, operating since 2014. They specialise in delivering goods across hospitality and healthcare sector, supported by a dedicated vehicle fleet delivering general freight, palletised freight, same-day/next-day services. They require dedicated experienced Office Manager to oversee the office and administrative backbone of the business.

Responsibilities
The Office Manager is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the daily administrative operations of the business, ensuring effective communication and workflow between office, warehouse, and fleet functions. The role involves developing and improving office systems, managing administrative staff, preparing rosters and schedules, recruitment and training, and maintaining efficient office resources. Manages budgets, financial records, and compliance requirements to support smooth freight operations, fleet administration, and the overall performance of the business.

Key Duties 
•	Plan, organise, direct and coordinate the day-to-day administrative operations of the business office, managing office procedures, correspondence, office records, and information flow between administration, dispatch, and fleet teams.
•	Develop, implement and review office systems, policies and administrative procedures to improve operational efficiency, document control, customer service processes, and internal communication across the business.
•	Liaise and coordinate with administrative staff and director, prepare workflow, and coordinate workload requirements to support freight, delivery, and business operations.
•	Oversee recruitment, onboarding, induction, and training coordination for office staffs, ensuring staff are appropriately supported and aligned with company procedures and operational requirements.
•	Maintain supplier records, and other administrative information systems to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and compliance with company requirements.
•	Manage office budgets, process financial administration activities, monitor expenditure, coordinate invoicing and accounts administration, and maintain financial records in conjunction with management and external accountant.
•	Coordinate procurement, inventory control, and distribution of office supplies, stationery, equipment, and administrative resources to ensure the office operates efficiently and effectively.
•	Manage communication with suppliers and internal stakeholders, including handling enquiries, and supporting service delivery requirements for the customers.
•	Coordinate workplace facilities, office equipment, and administrative service requirements and supplier services to support a safe and productive working environment.
•	Monitor administrative compliance requirements, maintain company documentation, support audits and reporting processes, and provide management with administrative information to assist decision-making.

Required Qualification & Experience
•	Minimum AQF Associate Diploma or Higher-level Degree in related field; and
•	A minimum of 1-year relevant experience

Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum, commensurate with skills and experience.

Application Timeframe: 28 July 2026 to 27 August 2026. 
Interested candidates should submit their resume and cover letter. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the interview.

result.description:
Chef

Business: The Malaya
Location: The Rocks NSW 2000
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $80,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

Full Job DescriptionAbout the Business

The Malaya is one of Sydney's most iconic and award-winning restaurants, renowned for its distinctive blend of Southeast Asian cuisine inspired by Malaysian, Chinese, Thai, Indonesian, and Indian culinary traditions. Located at 225 George Street, The Rocks NSW 2000, the restaurant has built an outstanding reputation for delivering exceptional dining experiences through premium-quality cuisine, innovative flavours, and outstanding customer service.

Operating within Sydney's highly competitive premium dining and hospitality industry, The Malaya provides lunch and dinner services, private dining, corporate functions, special events, and takeaway options to a diverse clientele comprising local residents, business professionals, domestic and international tourists, and corporate customers. Maintaining exceptional food quality, efficient kitchen operations, and consistently high service standards is fundamental to the restaurant's continued success and reputation.

Due to continued customer demand and ongoing business growth, The Malaya is seeking to appoint a dedicated Chef to support the efficient operation of its commercial kitchen and contribute to maintaining its high culinary standards.

About the Role

The Chef is responsible for planning, organising, and coordinating the preparation and cooking of food while ensuring consistently high standards of quality, presentation, food safety, and operational efficiency. The position plays a key role in supporting daily kitchen operations, supervising food preparation activities, maintaining inventory levels, and ensuring efficient service delivery during busy trading periods.

The successful applicant will demonstrate exceptional culinary skills, strong organisational ability, leadership capability, and the ability to perform effectively within a high-volume premium commercial kitchen specialising in authentic Southeast Asian cuisine.

Key Responsibilities

The successful applicant will be responsible for:

Planning menus in consultation with management while considering customer demand, seasonal availability, and operational requirements.
Estimating food and labour costs and assisting with kitchen budgeting and cost control.
Ordering food supplies, monitoring inventory levels, rotating stock, and minimising food wastage.
Preparing, cooking, seasoning, and presenting high-quality dishes in accordance with established recipes and presentation standards.
Monitoring the quality of dishes throughout all stages of preparation, cooking, and presentation.
Discussing food preparation requirements and operational issues with management and kitchen staff to ensure efficient workflow.
Demonstrating cooking techniques and providing guidance to junior kitchen employees.
Supervising food preparation activities to ensure consistency, efficiency, and compliance with company procedures.
Ensuring compliance with food safety legislation, HACCP principles, workplace health and safety requirements, and hygiene regulations.
Maintaining cleanliness and organisation of kitchen facilities, equipment, and food preparation areas.
Assisting in the selection, training, and supervision of kitchen employees.
Freezing, storing, preserving, and handling food products in accordance with food safety standards.
Supporting efficient kitchen operations during peak service periods while maintaining exceptional food quality and customer satisfaction.
Requirements

Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents are encouraged to apply.

Applicants should possess:

AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Commercial Cookery, Hospitality Management, or a closely related discipline;
OR

At least three years of relevant commercial kitchen experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
Applicants should also demonstrate:

Experience working as a Chef within a commercial restaurant or premium hospitality environment.
Strong menu planning and food preparation skills, particularly within Asian or contemporary cuisine.
Knowledge of food costing, stock management, and inventory control.
Thorough understanding of HACCP, food safety legislation, and workplace health and safety requirements.
Excellent leadership, communication, and organisational skills.
Ability to supervise kitchen staff and coordinate kitchen workflow.
Ability to perform efficiently within a fast-paced, high-volume commercial kitchen.
Strong commitment to food quality, presentation, consistency, and customer satisfaction.
Work Conditions

Rotating roster including weekends, evenings, and public holidays.
Opportunity to work within one of Sydney's most prestigious and long-established restaurants with ongoing career development opportunities.
Note: Preference will be given to suitably qualified Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents.

Job Types: Full-time, Permanent

Work Location: In person

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Senior Medical Services Support Officer



 Apply now
 Job no: 943953

 Work type: Full time

 Location: Adelaide Hills

 Categories: Administration, Business and Management, Support Services





 

Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network

Medical Administration - Position location negotiable within region

Salary: $82,212 per annum - $86,180 per annum - adjusted to hours worked

Full-Time, Ongoing - start August 2026

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

The Senior Medical Services Support Officer role oversees and supports a team of Medical Services Liaison Officers to deliver efficient, high-quality administrative and coordination services across medical departments. You will provide clear direction, mentoring and development to ensure alignment with organisational priorities, while managing key functions including rostering, timesheets, credentialing, recruitment and onboarding of Medical Officers. The role also leads the preparation of accurate, confidential correspondence and reporting, and promotes effective communication and stakeholder engagement.

You will drive service improvement by monitoring performance, streamlining processes, and ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and best practice. Working closely with clinical leadership, you will support workforce planning, locum coordination, visa processes, and mandatory training compliance, while contributing to operational planning and reporting. This role offers the opportunity to strengthen team capability, foster a positive culture, and enhance the delivery of safe, effective and patient-centred medical services.

WHO ARE WE? 

The Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network offers opportunities across our sites, from Kangaroo Island to Eudunda, wrapping all the way around our metropolitan areas. We pride ourselves on providing exceptional care to all our consumers, residents, their families, and community. Our mission is to ensure that you always receive the best quality, safe, consistent, collaborative care and always with kindness. We do this by maintaining exceptional levels of care at all times supported by systems and processes that assure us of quality and safety of our staff and those we serve.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

Are you motivated to lead and develop a high-performing administrative team, providing clear direction, support and accountability?

Do you thrive on improving systems and processes to deliver efficient, accurate and high-quality outcomes?

Are you driven to build strong relationships and communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders?

Do you take pride in ensuring compliance, accuracy and attention to detail across complex administrative functions?

Are you passionate about contributing to a positive workplace culture and supporting safe, patient-centred healthcare delivery?

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will.... 

Lead and support Medical Services Liaison Officers to deliver efficient, high-quality administrative and coordination services.

Oversee rostering, timesheet management, credentialing, and onboarding processes for Medical Officers.

Coordinate recruitment activities, including locum engagement, contracts, and workforce planning support. 

Monitor performance, ensure compliance with policies and standards, and drive process improvements. 

Support clinical leadership with reporting, operational planning, and the delivery of safe, patient-centred services.

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways:

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT yearClick here more information

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities.

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families.

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS? 

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following:

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy.Further information is in the application for to help guide you. 

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description.

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. We continually look for ways to support and promote diversity and flexible ways of working so please let us know what interests you. 

NEED TO RELOCATE? 

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. See what is available here:Relocation support | SA Health.Find out more about working in theBarossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network, and see what it looks like to work and live in regional Australia at:https:--movetomore.com.au-

HELP IS HERE! 

Please refer to all the details in the Role Description below (job ref: 943953), or reach out to Tracey Stone, A-Business Manager, Medical Services on phone: 0403 662 832 or email: tracy.stone@sa.gov.au

To find out what you need to apply, and what is required to be offered a role, please refer to the Applicant ChecklistBHFLHN Applicant Checklist.pdf. Please also click here for ourAustralian applicant guidelines

FIND OUT MORE ABOUT OUR NETWORK 

Stay connected with our Network! Follow us onLinkedInto stay informed about exciting job opportunities and updates on us and what our employees are doing.Click hereto join the conversation.

-Visa sponsors, will support permanent residency.

ADDITIONAL BENEFITS
-Relocation / Sign-on bonus available

ABOUT YOU
-This role will suit a General Practitioner who holds FRACGP, FACRRM, or a comparable specialist pathway qualification

INVENTORY CONCEPTS
Pymble, Sydney, NSW 2073

Full Time Contract Administrator
SALARY:  $87,500 per annum plus superannuation 

Position 
The Contract Administrator is responsible for the administration, performance monitoring, and commercial management of all client contracts and fixed-rate service agreements across the business. The role plays a critical part in ensuring contractual compliance, maintaining profitability, protecting contract margins and compliance, and delivering operational efficiencies throughout the supply chain and logistics network. 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Contract Administration and Commercial Management 
•	Administer and manage all client contracts and fixed-price service agreements to ensure compliance with contractual obligations and service level requirements. 
•	Monitor contract performance, profitability, and operational outcomes against agreed contractual terms. 
•	Develop, review, negotiate, and implement contract variations, renewals, extensions, and service agreements. 
•	Identify and implement initiatives to improve contract profitability and operational efficiency. 
•	Maintain accurate contract documentation, pricing schedules, and commercial records. 
Financial Analysis and Business Improvement 
•	Analyse operational, financial, and performance data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for cost reduction and productivity improvements. 
•	Develop pricing models and costing structures for existing and prospective contracts. 
•	Prepare costing and pricing inputs for contract renewals, variations and client quotation responses. 
•	Conduct commercial analysis of contract performance to support contract negotiations, variations and renewals. 
•	Prepare forecasting data and performance reports to support future business planning. 
Client and Stakeholder Management 
•	Build and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective clients. 
•	Act as a key point of contact for contractual matters and service-related issues. 
•	Ensure client expectations and contractual deliverables are clearly understood and consistently achieved. 
•	Support client retention initiatives and identify opportunities to expand service offerings within existing contracts. 
•	Participate in contract review meetings with clients, subcontractors and management. 
Supply Chain and Operational Coordination 
•	Work closely with logistics, warehouse, and inventory management teams to ensure contractual requirements are effectively delivered. 
•	Coordinate subcontractor performance to ensure service delivery standards, compliance requirements, and commercial objectives are achieved. 
•	Monitor operational performance against contractual KPIs and agreed service levels. 
•	Assist in the implementation of continuous improvement initiatives across supply chain operations.
Contract Compliance, Risk and Reporting 
•	Analyse risks associated with specific contract terms and advise management on appropriate mitigation. 
•	Monitor relevant legislative, award and regulatory changes affecting contracts and coordinate with management and external advisers as required. 
•	Interpret and explain contract requirements, terms and conditions to internal stakeholders, clients and subcontractors to support compliance. 
•	Maintain and improve contract-management systems and records, including the in-house platform, to support accurate and efficient contract administration. 
•	Assist in the preparation and negotiation of contract terms, renewals and variations with clients and subcontractors. 

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, AND EXPERIENCE 
•	Demonstrated experience in contract administration, commercial management, or supply chain contract management. 
•	Strong financial and commercial acumen with the ability to analyse costs, profitability, and operational performance. 
•	Experience within logistics, warehousing, inventory management, third-party logistics (3PL), or supply chain environments. 
•	Sound understanding of fixed-price service agreements, contract compliance, and service level management. 
•	Proven ability to manage multiple stakeholders and maintain strong client relationships. 
•	Experience in pricing analysis, contract negotiation, and the administration of contract variations and renewals. 
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with advanced data interpretation capabilities. 
•	Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
•	High-level computer literacy and proficiency in business systems, reporting tools, and data analysis software. 
•	Knowledge of warehouse operations, distribution centres, inventory control, container handling, and material handling equipment (MHE). 
•	Demonstrated understanding of Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) requirements within 
•	logistics and distribution environments. 
•	Relevant qualifications in Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations 
•	Management, Information Technology, or a related discipline at AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma level or above. 
•	A demonstrable track record in WHS and its applications in fast paced and dynamic distribution facilities. 


Applications open on 24 July 2026 and close on 23 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.
